record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: If I is a square-free monomial ideal such that S/I is Gorenstein, does the h-vector of S/I satisfy the numerical conditions from the g-Theorem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S = k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $I \subseteq S$ be a square-free monomial ideal (equivalently, the Stanley–Reisner ideal of some simplicial complex $\Delta$ on vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$), and assume that the quotient ring $S/I$ is Gorenstein. Let $d = \dim(S/I)$ and write the Hilbert series of $S/I$ as
$$\mathrm{Hilb}_{S/I}(t) = \frac{h_0 + h_1 t + \cdots + h_s t^s}{(1-t)^d},$$
so $(h_0, h_1, \ldots, h_s)$ is the $h$-vector of $S/I$.

Recall the $g$-theorem conditions on an integer sequence $(h_0, h_1, \ldots, h_s)$ of length $s+1$:
(i) $h_0 = 1$ and $h_i = h_{s-i}$ for all $0 \le i \le s$ (symmetry/palindromy);
(ii) the associated $g$-vector defined by $g_0 = 1$ and $g_i = h_i - h_{i-1}$ for $1 \le i \le \lfloor s/2 \rfloor$ is an $M$-sequence (i.e., the Hilbert function of some standard graded Artinian $k$-algebra), equivalently it satisfies Macaulay's bound $0 \le g_i \le g_{i-1}^{\langle i-1 \rangle}$.

Question: Does the $h$-vector of every such Gorenstein quotient $S/I$ by a square-free monomial ideal satisfy conditions (i) and (ii) of the $g$-theorem?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a form of the $g$-conjecture for Gorenstein* simplicial complexes (equivalent to square-free Gorenstein quotients after taking the core). Symmetry of the $h$-vector is classical (Stanley). The unimodality and $M$-sequence (g-theorem) conditions for simplicial spheres / Gorenstein* complexes were established by K. Adiprasito (2018), which covers the case where $\Delta$ is a homology sphere. The general statement for arbitrary Gorenstein square-free monomial ideals reduces, via the core, to this Gorenstein* setting, so it is essentially resolved by Adiprasito's theorem, although the full literature still treats some aspects (e.g., effective constructions, characteristic-free statements) as active. The problem is therefore best described as partially solved / largely solved.

status_evidence.title: h-vector — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The g-conjecture stated that for simplicial spheres, all possible h-vectors occur ... It was proved in December 2018 by Karim Adiprasito.
status_evidence.claim: Adiprasito proved the g-theorem for simplicial spheres, which covers Gorenstein* Stanley–Reisner rings.

status_evidence.title: Stanley, f-vectors and h-vectors of simplicial posets
status_evidence.snippet: Stanley conjectures characterizing f-vectors of Gorenstein* simplicial posets/complexes via g-theorem conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The g-theorem characterization of h-vectors of Gorenstein* complexes is the conjecture relevant to square-free Gorenstein monomial ideals.
